title: Finite generating sections are detected by their stalk spans
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $M$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module. Let $I$ be a finite set and $s_i$ a family of global sections. Using the stalk modules and germs of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], the sections generate $M$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] if and only if, for every $y\in Y$, the $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-span of the germs $s_{i,y}$ is all of $M_y$.

source.place: Modules Definition 01AM; Sheaves Lemma 0H7H(2); the finite direct-sum stalk calculation is step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre.

proof.text: Form the free sheaf morphism f associated to the sections. On every open U its i-th component sends a to a times s_i restricted to U. This follows from unitHomEquiv and freeHomEquiv.

The map on stalks is linear over the ring stalk. The identity on the finite free sheaf is the sum of the inclusions composed with coordinate projections (sum_freeπ_ιFree). Represent a stalk element by a section; applying this identity, f, and the germ map writes its image as a sum of coefficient germs times s_{i,y}. Conversely each s_{i,y} is the image of the germ of the i-th basis section. Thus the linear stalk map has range equal to the span of the germs.

The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves colimits and hence epimorphisms. The abelian-sheaf stalk functor is a left adjoint and hence preserves epimorphisms. Epimorphisms of abelian groups are surjective, proving the forward direction. Conversely, range equal to top makes each stalk map surjective; epi_of_surjective_stalk, using the local-surjectivity criterion, gives the reverse direction.

lean.statement: theorem generating_sections_iff_stalk_span (Y : Scheme.{u}) (M : Y.Modules) {I : Type u} [Finite I] (s : I → M.sections) : Epi (M.freeHomEquiv.symm s) ↔ ∀ y : Y, Submodule.span (Y.presheaf.stalk y) (Set.range fun i ↦ (TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf ⊤ y trivial) ((s i).val (Opposite.op ⊤))) = ⊤
